# ASIG 0.6.0 review evidence

Stable 0.6.0 release preparation. The development-stage evidence below was collected for
0.6.0-dev.0. Existing consumers retain their pinned version until explicitly upgraded.

## Implementation

Adds an agent design brief, opt-in typography roles, generated foundations gallery,
copy/search/theme interactions and a sample-only Operations composition. The opt-in labeled
module rail reflects the current ERP's outline icons, visible labels and module tones.
Native form controls can shrink within narrow grid tracks at enlarged text sizes.
No ERP business rule is changed by this candidate.

## Initial candidate automated verification

Local Chromium run: `npm test -- --workers=4` passed 148 tests; 40 intentional
viewport-specific skips. Includes responsive/theme snapshots, clipboard success/failure,
token search, sample validation/recovery, module switching and destination icon updates,
visible keyboard focus, Axe scans and 320px reflow with 200% text for the new guide pages.
Navigation identity token pairs are checked for at least 4.5:1 contrast across all four themes.
`npm run check` passed source, generated output, deterministic snapshot and package checks.
`npm audit --audit-level=high` reported zero vulnerabilities.
Mac and Linux Chromium reference images were generated for all 26 visual cases. Linux
generation used a local emulated Playwright container, not hosted CI: the first run encountered
capture timeouts. New screenshot assertions now allow 40 seconds, consistent with the existing
catalogue assertion. All four desktop navigation cases passed their focused Linux rerun;
the dark foundations reference needed one retry. Hosted CI is still unverified. After the
accessible Ops label adjustment, 20 affected local interaction/visual cases passed again.
Automated checks do not establish complete accessibility conformance.

## Human verification

- Browser visual review: foundations, Operations composition and labeled navigation inspected;
  narrow/wide light and dark navigation captures reviewed. Browser module switching and Tab
  focus checked. This is a scoped review, not exhaustive assistive-technology testing.
- Screen reader/browser combinations: pending human review.
- OS forced colors, zoom and reduced transparency: pending human review; emulation is
  separate regression evidence.
- ERP, CAD and Marketing adoption/UAT: separate product work, not certified here.

## September 22 page-design extension

Added eleven operational typography roles and layout/density tokens, opt-in pages.css,
a generated visual page guide, and Orders/Workbench/order-detail examples. Both CSS
entry points now include typography (previously omitted from the flat bundle).

Local full run: `npm test -- --workers=4 --max-failures=3` passed 212 tests with 56 intentional
viewport-specific skips. New coverage includes light/dark, loading/empty/error/restricted
previews, sample filtering/sorting, task counts, validation/retry retention, bundle parity
and 320px reflow with 200% text. Horizontal table clipping can prevent Axe from sampling
offscreen cell contrast; only those specific incomplete nodes are allowed, and full-width
runs check the same columns. All other uncertain contrast fails the new page checks.

Browser review inspected the guide, Orders, Workbench and detail hierarchy. It caught and
fixed primary-link color inheritance and excessively narrow table columns. Tables now
scroll within their region and order identifiers remain on one line. Reference controls
are placed in a native disclosure. Product adoption, persistence and human screen-reader
UAT remain separate and are not claimed by these sample pages.

The combined bundle now derives its file order from all.css, eliminating the separate list
that omitted typography. Generated-output checks and the browser parity test cover it.
The final targeted page run passed all 48 cases after the identifier and stylesheet-load
checks were tightened. Source/package/snapshot checks also passed.

Linux references: all 16 new page/theme/viewport captures completed. Final Orders captures
passed a four-case rerun. The existing tablet/desktop catalogue captures required retries
in local QEMU emulation; their isolated rerun passed both cases with a temporary 120-second
capture allowance. Repository snapshot tolerances remain unchanged. Hosted CI was not run.
Browser inspection covered representative layouts at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px, including
mobile table scrolling and desktop dark mode. The reference pages are still sample-only.

## September 22 review corrections

Excluded skip links from the page-level anchor color override. The four page references now
test the first keyboard stop, focused skip-link contrast in both themes, and Enter moving
focus to the main landmark at all four viewport sizes.

Guidance links now use an HTML reading view that displays canonical Markdown as inert text.
This also avoids the in-app browser's block on direct Markdown navigation. Direct Markdown
requests receive a plain-text content type. Browser checks cover guidance navigation, narrow
reflow, automated accessibility, literal HTML in source, and unavailable-document recovery.
The preview server also redirects directory URLs so `/site` and `/` resolve relative assets.

Final local Chromium run: `npm test -- --workers=4` passed 224 tests with 56 intentional skips.
In-app browser inspection confirmed the readable focused skip link and the guidance reader.
The candidate remains `0.6.0-dev.0`; no npm publication, hosted CI or product UAT is claimed.

## Stable 0.6.0 release preparation

The maintainer selected 0.6.0 as the stable release. Package versions, token JSON, peer
dependency, install examples and the vendored snapshot are aligned. Stable publication
uses `latest`; the release gate continues to test prerelease routing to `next`.

The final local Chromium suite passed 229 tests with 59 intentional viewport-specific skips.
Source, generated output, package contents and deterministic snapshot checks passed.
GitHub workflow syntax and the new documentation links were checked. The public wiki
contains six guides with a shared sidebar and footer, and its sources are tracked in
`.github/wiki/`. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled.

The human verification items above remain pending; stable versioning does not certify
screen-reader compatibility or product UAT. Hosted workflow results, registry versions
and provenance must be verified against the release commit after publication.

The stable-version Linux visual reference run passed 12 cases with 8 intentional skips.
Local x86 emulation needed a temporary 180-second test limit and 120-second foundations
capture limit; repository CI timeouts and screenshot tolerances remain unchanged.
The reviewed reference changes reflect the stable version label and updated release text.
